senses.definition: (transitive) To inhabit or to visit frequently (most often used in reference to ghosts).
examples: A couple of ghosts haunt the old, burnt-down house.

quotes.text: You wrong me Sir,thus ſtill to haunt my houſe.

quotes.text: Foul spirits haunt my resting place.

quotes.text: those cares that haunt the court and town
quotes.reference: 1713, Jonathan Swift, Imitation of Horace, Book I. Ep. VII:

examples: The memory of his past failures haunted him.

quotes.text: The murder of Déagol haunted Gollum, and he had made up a defence.
quotes.reference: 1954, J.R.R. Tolkien, The Fellowship of the Ring:

examples: The policeman haunted him, following him everywhere.

senses.definition: (intransitive, now rare) To live habitually; to stay, to remain.

quotes.text: Ieſus therfore walked no more openly amõge the iewes : butt went his waye thence vnto a countre ny to a wildernes into a cite called effraym / and there haunted with his diſciples.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To persist in staying or visiting.

quotes.text: I haue charg’d thee not to haunt about my doores:[…]

senses.definition: A place at which one is regularly found; a habitation or hangout.
examples: The shopping mall is a popular haunt of the local teenagers in this town.
I went back the town I used to live and visited all my old haunts.

quotes.text: It is a great rock or cliff on the loneliest part of the mountains, and, … is known by the name of the Garden Rock. Near the foot of it is a small lake, the haunt of the solitary bittern, with water-snakes basking in the sun on the leaves of the pond-lilies which lie on the surface.
